candidates.summary: Hundreds of fans went to Robin Park Arena to sign a book of condolence for the Wigan Warriors star

candidates.lead: Hundreds of fans went to Robin Park Arena to sign a book of condolence for the Wigan Warriors star
candidates.evidence_text: Fans share memories of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston - BBC News Image caption, Hundreds of fans have paid tribute to Sir Billy Boston by signing the book of condolence at Robin Park Arena By Yunus Mulla Reporting from Wigan Published 1 hour ago Fans have shared memories of the much-loved rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston and signed a book of condolence at his former club Wigan Warriors. Rugby league's first knight died earlier this week aged 92 surrounded by his closest family, the club said. As well as his achievements on the pitch - including scoring 571 tries in his career - a total surpassed only by Australian legend Brian Bevan in top-class rugby league - Boston has a legion of fans heartbroken at the legend's death. The club's kitman, and a lifelong fan who first saw him as a child, and decades later worked for him in his pub when he retired, were among hundreds who went to Robin Park Arena to pay tribute to the star. Image source, PA Media Image caption, Billy Boston who was rugby league's first knight died on Tuesday aged 92 Josie Andrews held back the tears as she told BBC North West Tonight : "I fell in love with Billy Boston when I was eight. "My dad took me to watch him and that is when I fell in love with Wigan rugby." She said she later worked for Boston when he ran the Griffin Hotel close to Wigan's Central Park Ground after he retired from the game. Image caption, Josie Andrews fought back tears as she described how she fell in love with him when her dad took her to watch him at eight Another fan paying his respects was David Mullen who said he met the great man twice and described him as an "absolute gent". "At the ground we always saw Sir Billy and what an absolute guy he was." Image caption, David Mullen Standard bearer for Royal British Legion and met him twice He added: "I met him twice because I was a standard-bearer for the branch of the Royal British Legion and when they had the military here, I've been in the tunnel and met him then." "You couldn't wish to meet a nicer guy." Image caption, Kitman Roy Dickinson said Billy Boston was his first sporting hero and still is The club's kitman, Roy Dickinson, said: "Billy was my first sporting hero, and he still is. Always will be." He said he shared some good times with the legend in the Griffin Hotel and treasured a photograph taken in there with Boston. "We used to go in Billy's pub... and the old players used to go in at that time." Image source, Family photograph Image caption, Roy Dickinson (far right) pictured with Billy Boston (centre) in the star's pub, the Griffin Hotel, in the 1980s He laughed as he recalled how Boston played darts in the pub. "He used to get more nervous playing darts than he did playing at Wembley." Image caption, Geoff Hallewell said Sir Billy Boston and his wife Lady Joan were always "so welcoming" and had "no airs" Geoff Hallewell said he often shared a table with Billy at club events and their wives were friends. "He told us all about his childhood, where he was brought up in Angelina Street in Cardiff." Hallewell said his wife and Lady Joan, who died a month before Boston, had known each other for a long time. "They were always so welcoming, both of them. No airs about them at all. "Billy was the greatest rugby player ever, but he didn't realise it, I don't think." Image caption, Michael Lyall travelled from Chorley to Wigan to sign Sir Billy Boston's book of condolence Michael Lyall said he travelled from Chorley, Lancashire, to sign the book of condolence. "He was great, brilliant, just the job. "I wish he'd played for Rhinos, though." You can also send story ideas via Whatsapp to 0808 100 2230. candidates.evidence_text: Peter Kay is to perform a one-off show in Blackpool next month to raise funds for a teenager's vital heart operation Fin Cormack, from Prenton, Merseyside, has a rare condition called Ebstein's anomaly and has had several major heart surgeries, with his first when he was just 11 days old Now 19, his family are trying to pay for treatment for him in the United States and the Bolton comedian said he was inspired to do the special show at the Opera House in Blackpool's Winter Gardens on 27 September after seeing his story on the news Fin's mum said the family were "bowled over" by the star's incredible gesture Ebstein's anomaly is an abnormality of the tricuspid valve that you were born with, according to the NHS The family said they were trying to raise £200,000 for treatment from a leading expert on the condition, Dr Dearani, at the Mayo Clinic in the USA, "to give Fin something he's never really had: the chance at a fuller, easier life"

candidates.lead: People using the George House Trust are told personal health information may have been compromised
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester HIV charity has 'sensitive' health data stolen - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, George House Trust said it informed people affected once the situation became clear By Mat Trewern North West Published 26 August 2026 People using an HIV charity have been told their "sensitive and personal" health information may have been stolen in a data breach. In an email sent to George House Trust users and seen by the BBC, the Manchester-based organisation said the material had been downloaded by hackers but not published. The breach is part of a wider cyber security incident potentially affecting up to 1,500 charities across the UK. George House Trust said it was investigating and "taking all appropriate steps". The charity, which was set up in 1985, provides support, advice and information to thousands of people living with HIV. It is unclear how many people connected to the trust have been affected by the breach. The email said personal information including addresses, emails, telephone numbers and "notes and records" about users engagement with the charity was on the database that was targeted. However, it said there was "no sign that any of the data or information" had been "misused in any way at this time". Review carried out The security incident involves technology company Beacon, which operates a database system used by more than a thousand charities across the country. Beacon said the data breach happened at the end of July and it "immediately engaged external cyber security experts to help contain the incident and investigate". The company said it was supporting all the organisations affected. George House Trust said it was informed by Beacon about the breach on 3 August, although it was three weeks later that affected users were told. The charity said it had waited until it had a "fuller understanding" of what had happened" before informing people. In a statement, the charity said it had conducted a review of the data that Beacon holds and, where it identified sensitive data, it had "sought to inform the relevant individuals". candidates.lead: Dove Stone reservoir has reopened after firefighters spent more than three weeks tackling a wildfire
candidates.evidence_text: Dove Stone residents fear parking 'nightmare' after beauty spot reopens - BBC News Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, The beauty spot has been plagued by parking problems, such as here in April 2026 By Ed Barnes , Local Democracy Reporting Service and Haider Saleem , North West , Reporting from North West Published 26 August 2026 People living near a Greater Manchester beauty spot fear a return to a "nightmare" of car-jammed roads and litter after the area reopened following a wildfire. Dove Stone reservoir, near Greenfield in Oldham reopened last week after the blaze burned for more than three weeks. Residents said the area had previously been plagued by obstructed roads, while visitors also left litter and lit barbecues, raising concerns about access for emergency vehicles - and now they fear a return of the same issues. Oldham Council said wardens patrolled the area and issued 946 penalty charge notices around the reservoir in 2025. The RSPB, which manages the attraction's car park, said it understood the concerns. The wildfire began on 11 July and was declared a major incident, with people told to avoid the area while firefighters tackled the blaze. The incident was stood down on 3 August, although crews remained at the scene for days afterwards. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Visitors are being urged to respect the landscape and take their litter home Karen O'Connor, who has lived near the reservoir for 35 years, said increasing visitor numbers had made conditions worse - and she worried about emergency access. "It was never like this," she said. "It takes forever getting out. They just abandon the cars anywhere. "If something happened to someone up here, they would just be stranded." Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Natalie Wilde said litter and barbecues had been persistent problems around the reservoir Another resident, Natalie Wilde, said litter and barbecues had been persistent problems. "They can see the signs. They just do not listen," she said. "They need to be more on top of things. Put more bins out especially around Dovestone. Put more signs around to deter barbecues and fires." Barbecues, campfires and fireworks are prohibited at the reserve, where visitors have been warned about the risk of wildfire. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, The RSPB took on the operation of Dovestone car park in summer 2026 The main car park has 117 spaces and four blue badge bays, according to the RSPB. Councillor Helen Bishop, who represents Saddleworth South, said it was "great" that people could visit the reservoir again but she had "deep-rooted concerns" that it had reopened too soon. She said a comprehensive plan covering the safety of residents, visitors, wildlife and the environment should have been agreed and communicated first. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Dove Stone reservoir reopened to visitors on 20 August The RSPB said high visitor numbers brought benefits for well-being, access to nature and local tourism, but also created challenges. It urged visitors to park considerately, take their litter home and respect the landscape and nearby residents. The charity said it was working with United Utilities, Oldham Council and local communities on longer-term plans for the site. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, The area is a popular walking spot A council spokesperson said permanent double yellow lines had been introduced to try to ease parking problems. "We want everyone to enjoy our green spaces and countryside – but we also ask that people respect the area and local residents," it said. "Sadly, problem parking is an issue at many beauty spots across the country, especially when the weather is good." candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police says drones are 'future of policing' - BBC News Image source, Greater Manchester Police Image caption, Police have been using drones to track down bike thieves across the north of Manchester By Richard Stead North West Published 26 August 2026 Drones have been described a "the future of policing" after they were used to help seize 130 illegal off-road bikes across north Manchester in the less than a year. The fleet of drones is being used by Greater Manchester Police instead of the force helicopter because drones are cheaper to use and more discreet. Insp Dan Pickavance, from GMP's North Manchester Neighbourhood Policing Team, said: "All police forces can use drones - particularly in urban areas - and it means we can safely take illegal off-road bikes off the streets. "Using drones is without doubt the future of neighbourhood policing and this is an essential game-changer for us going forward." Image caption, Dan Pickavance, a neighbourhood police inspector for North Manchester, was able to monitor the images from the drone The BBC followed a police operation in which a drone was used to recover a stolen bike that had been spotted in Boggart Hole Clough. The drone was used to follow the bike to an address in nearby Charlestown, where police officers on the ground searched the property and arrested three suspects. The operation was directed by a senior police officer in the back of a van, using live images from the drone which were relayed onto a screen. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, Drones are a "game-changer", police say Some of the drones can operate safely in storms, at speeds of up to 40mph (64km/h), and are equipped with thermal imaging technology so they can be used in the dark. The drones come in various sizes, costing between £6,000 and £30,000. candidates.evidence_text: Peter Kay is to perform a one-off show in Blackpool next month to raise funds for a teenager's vital heart operation Fin Cormack, from Prenton, Merseyside, has a rare condition called Ebstein's anomaly and has had several major heart surgeries, with his first when he was just 11 days old Now 19, his family are trying to pay for treatment for him in the United States and the Bolton comedian said he was inspired to do the special show at the Opera House in Blackpool's Winter Gardens on 27 September after seeing his story on the news Fin's mum said the family were "bowled over" by the star's incredible gesture Ebstein's anomaly is an abnormality of the tricuspid valve that you were born with, according to the NHS The family said they were trying to raise £200,000 for treatment from a leading expert on the condition, Dr Dearani, at the Mayo Clinic in the USA, "to give Fin something he's never really had: the chance at a fuller, easier life"

Back in 2019, aged 35, he and his wife had offered to take a friend's young son for a day out at a soft play centre in Manchester - as they often did Amid the children's laughter and noise, he began to feel as though something wasn't quite right. "He was off playing," Martin said. "I'd gone back to my wife, got drinks or something, and then I went back to find him "And as I've seen him, I've gone towards him, and I've ducked under a bridge that was in there. Martin, who works in IT for the NHS, describes the sensation as his heart 'skipping a beat', adding: "I didn't feel great so I went back to my wife and I'm like, I don't feel good, I don't feel right."

The 57-year-old believes the issue is caused by an unused pipe that has been funnelling waste water into his But United Utilities say wastewater from their system has not entered James' home, and is instead 'ground water' linked to historical problems with his property James moved into the Denton home back in 1996. However, he claims issues started to arise by 2000. He told the MEN he uncovered an unused underground pipe behind his home that he believes was the source of the flooding that was blighting his property James says he has approached United Utilities several times over the situation. " My floor and my hallway fell into what used to be the cellar."

Concerns were triggered at around 9.49am on November 9 following the discovery of a body beside the tracks Sergeant Adam Goodall was amongst the first police officers on the scene. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Tragedy as dad, 28, found dead 18 hours after leaving for party in Manchester Ethan Joseph had struggled with his mental health prior to his death News Thomas Cooper and Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 07:53, 27 Aug 2026 View Imag A dad tragically took his own life on railway tracks after leaving for a close friend's party in Manchester Ethan Joseph, 28, was found dead on train tracks in North Staffordshire on November 9. The previous day, he had left his Newcastle-under-Lyme home at around 2pm to head to Manchester for his friend's party But Ethan tragically took his own life before returning home. Concerns were triggered at around 9.49am on November 9 following the discovery of a body beside the tracks Sergeant Adam Goodall was amongst the first police officers on the scene. He told Ethan's inquest: "I arrived at around 10.28am. I could see that paramedics from West Midlands Ambulance Service and Network Rail workers were already on the scene "I was informed that life had already been pronounced extinct. Paramedics could see the patient had suffered injuries incompatible with life and consistent with being struck by a train.", reports Stoke on Trent Live

Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07: A row over the future of Market Street has taken another twist after a second petition was launched, making demands of the council The new petition has just nine signatures so far and is calling to ‘protect and support Market Street stalls’ and ‘keep fresh sweetcorn in the city centre’ It comes after another petition was launched last month calling for a review of Market Street and Piccadilly Gardens . The petition, which more than 600 people have put their names to, calls for a major revamp of the space to make it more organised and easier to use and tackle th Now, a new petition seeking to support traders has been set up by Muhammad Adnan. It states: "Market Street food stalls are part of what makes Manchester city centre special. They provide affordable, fresh sweetcorn and street food for families, workers, and tourists "Removing them takes away vibrancy, jobs, and choice. We the people of Manchester ask Manchester City Council to protect and support Market Street stalls."

candidates.evidence_text: Stockport The £41m row between Stagecoach and Stockport council Stagecoach said they were having 'positive discussions' but Stockport council has accused them of asking for too much money for two depots Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Repo Stagecoach is being accused of holding up major plans to revive Stockport town centre, amid claims the bus company asking for too much money. The issue is now being escalated by Stockport council over fears more than £40m could be lost The Stockport 8 development is one of the largest town centre regeneration projects in the UK. It could see over £350m of investment, and include 1,300 homes as well as new businesses It is part of plans by Stockport Council to completely transform the town with thousands of new homes The development covers a large area to the west of the town’s iconic railway viaduct between the now-finished Weir Mill scheme and the central railway station. Phase 1 of the scheme will include a mixed residential neighbourhood of 435 homes and 82 affordable properties It was hoped the first phase of the scheme would start construction in 2026 but the plans could now be delayed. This is because Stagecoach are asking for too much money in relation to their depots in the town centre, according to a new Stockport council report

After going into sudden heart failure, gaining seven stone from fear, and battl Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 05:52, 27 Aug 2026 Martin Buckley's story is the fourteenth in the Manchester Evening News' Survivors series, featuring interviews with remarkable people who have survived traumatic experiences Many never get the chance to hear terrifying news, doctors told Martin. Back in 2019, aged 35, he and his wife had offered to take a friend's young son for a day out at a soft play centre in Manchester - as they often did Amid the children's laughter and noise, he began to feel as though something wasn't quite right. "He was off playing," Martin said. "I'd gone back to my wife, got drinks or something, and then I went back to find him "And as I've seen him, I've gone towards him, and I've ducked under a bridge that was in there. As soon as I kind of bent down to go underneath it, something just happened in my heart." Martin, who works in IT for the NHS, describes the sensation as his heart 'skipping a beat', adding: "I didn't feel great so I went back to my wife and I'm like, I don't feel good, I don't feel right."

candidates.evidence_text: I've had no front doorway for over 12 months... it's been 26 years of hell' Dad-of-three James Johnstone blames a 26-year-old sewage leak for his problems, but United Utilities don't agree Family say they've been living above a sewer for 26 years Com Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , James Johnstone said he can no longer welcome guests through his front door after his hallway caved in during October last year. The 57-year-old believes the issue is caused by an unused pipe that has been funnelling waste water into his But United Utilities say wastewater from their system has not entered James' home, and is instead 'ground water' linked to historical problems with his property James moved into the Denton home back in 1996. However, he claims issues started to arise by 2000. He told the MEN he uncovered an unused underground pipe behind his home that he believes was the source of the flooding that was blighting his property James says he has approached United Utilities several times over the situation. And the dad-of-three says multiple engineers have carried out work on the system near his home, but nothing so far has addressed the main issue "I've had no front doorway for over a year," he said. " My floor and my hallway fell into what used to be the cellar."

candidates.summary: NHS Why NHS staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals have gone on strike Hospital staff say they are being pushed to work overtime for less money as staffing shortages, burnout and patient safety fears fuel an ongoing dispute with a Greater Manchest Outside Salford Royal, cars

candidates.evidence_text: NHS Why NHS staff at four Greater Manchester hospitals have gone on strike Hospital staff say they are being pushed to work overtime for less money as staffing shortages, burnout and patient safety fears fuel an ongoing dispute with a Greater Manchest Outside Salford Royal, cars honked in support of hundreds of NHS workers as they stood on the picket line in purple ponchos - and the rain poured Theatre staff at four NHS hospitals across Greater Manchester have walked out for a second day this week in an ongoing dispute about overtime pay More than 350 employees at Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust (NCA) - including nurses, clinical support workers and housekeepers - staged strike action on Monday (August 24) and Wednesday (August 26), and will walk out again on Friday (August 28) Those striking work across Salford Royal Hospital, Royal Oldham Hospital, Rochdale Infirmary and Fairfield Hospital in Bury It comes as the NCA has been criticised over patient safety concerns , with public records by the Trust showing dozens of patients have died or come to harm due to treatment delays and serious errors made by staff working under extreme pressure

Police later discovered a converted gun in a flat in Radcliffe where Hanson stored cocaine and cannabis for onward sale Previously, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it has launched an investigation into the firearms operation which ended in Hanson being shot During a sentencing hearing today, (August 26) Manchester Crown Court heard that Hanson, now 20, has been dealing cannabis since the age of 14, and had been trying to sell the gun prior to its seizure He will learn his fate tomorrow (August 27) after pleading guilty to drug and firearms charges. candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police GMP's facial recognition leads to first arrest from new alert system The LFR van was stationed at Manchester Victoria News Elizabeth Cotton TV and Celebrity Writer 17:55, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images A GMP van was deployed to Ma GMP’s latest Live Facial Recognition (LFR) operation led to several arrests on Wednesday, August 25, including the force’s first arrest following an alert linked to a Serious Crime Prevention Order The LFR van was stationed at Manchester Victoria throughout parts of the morning and afternoon, scanning the area for individuals on pre-set watchlists. These can include people wanted in connection with offences, registered sex offenders, missing people and others of interest Among those identified was a 46-year-old man who was arrested on suspicion of breaching a Serious Crime Prevention Order (SCPO), marking the first time an LFR alert has resulted in an arrest for an alleged SCPO breach Officers found the man carrying a number of mobile phones, tablets, passports and bank cards, which were believed to be in breach of conditions imposed on him by the courts. The items were seized and enquiries are continuing The operation also identified a man in his 40s who was wanted in connection with a theft dating back almost a year. He was subsequently arrested

Using a withheld number, he told the call receiver: "I'm going to come to your mosque and kill you." Police went to his home in Wakefield, West Yorkshire, just a few hours later and seized his mobile device. The CPS said it then emerged that a second threatening phone call was made Levy, who is Jewish, called the Iqra Mosque in Longsight on the same day and told a member of staff: "I am going to kill you Muslim" In a statement, the CPS said he admitted to being angry after watching news coverage of the October 2 synagogue attack, in which two men were killed at Heaton Park Hebrew Synagogue in Crumpsall. Levy pleaded guilty to making threats to kill and was sentenced on Wednesday at Leeds

candidates.evidence_text: Altrincham The north west’s 'best place to live' is about to get even better From ghost town to in demand, Altrincham has seen some changes over the years Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:42, 26 Aug 2026 View Image GV of Altrincham town centre (Imag Once criticised as empty, Altrincham is going from strength to strength with new plans have been unveiled to keep it growing In 2010, the Trafford market town was branded a ‘ghost town’ by the national press. A third of its shops stood empty – the highest vacancy rates in the UK – and one of its two main shopping centres, The Graftons, was in administration But Altrincham today is thriving. Its new position as a ‘top notch town’ saw it named the best place to live in the North West in this year’s The Sunday Times guide , with judges describing it as ‘classy, cool and effortlessly comfortable’ Seemingly, there is only more to come. Trafford council and developer Bruntwood have now announced a new £2.5m project to expand Foundation, which was completed in the Stamford Quarter in 2024 The building, which was once occupied by House of Fraser, is now a ‘collaborative workspace and leisure destination’. It has welcomed a number of leading national and independent brands since it opened

Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07: A row over the future of Market Street has taken another twist after a second petition was launched, making demands of the council The new petition has just nine signatures so far and is calling to ‘protect and support Market Street stalls’ and ‘keep fresh sweetcorn in the city centre’ It comes after another petition was launched last month calling for a review of Market Street and Piccadilly Gardens . The petition, which more than 600 people have put their names to, calls for a major revamp of the space to make it more organised and easier to use and tackle th Now, a new petition seeking to support traders has been set up by Muhammad Adnan. It states: "Market Street food stalls are part of what makes Manchester city centre special. They provide affordable, fresh sweetcorn and street food for families, workers, and tourists "Removing them takes away vibrancy, jobs, and choice. We the people of Manchester ask Manchester City Council to protect and support Market Street stalls."

candidates.evidence_text: I've had no front doorway for over 12 months... it's been 26 years of hell' Dad-of-three James Johnstone blames a 26-year-old sewage leak for his problems, but United Utilities don't agree Family say they've been living above a sewer for 26 years Com Speaking to the Manchester Evening News , James Johnstone said he can no longer welcome guests through his front door after his hallway caved in during October last year. The 57-year-old believes the issue is caused by an unused pipe that has been funnelling waste water into his But United Utilities say wastewater from their system has not entered James' home, and is instead 'ground water' linked to historical problems with his property James moved into the Denton home back in 1996. However, he claims issues started to arise by 2000. He told the MEN he uncovered an unused underground pipe behind his home that he believes was the source of the flooding that was blighting his property James says he has approached United Utilities several times over the situation. And the dad-of-three says multiple engineers have carried out work on the system near his home, but nothing so far has addressed the main issue "I've had no front doorway for over a year," he said. " My floor and my hallway fell into what used to be the cellar."

The issue is now being escalated by Stockport council over fears more than £40m could be lost The Stockport 8 development is one of the largest town centre regeneration projects in the UK. It could see over £350m of investment, and include 1,300 homes as well as new businesses It is part of plans by Stockport Council to completely transform the town with thousands of new homes The development covers a large area to the west of the town’s iconic railway viaduct between the now-finished Weir Mill scheme and the central railway station. Phase 1 of the scheme will include a mixed residential neighbourhood of 435 homes and 82 affordable properties It was hoped the first phase of the scheme would start construction in 2026 but the plans could now be delayed. This is because Stagecoach are asking for too much money in relation to their depots in the town centre, according to a new Stockport council report

candidates.evidence_text: Rochdale 'I thought I was going to drop dead': The NHS worker saved from a hidden 'widow maker' A day out at a soft play centre almost ended in tragedy for Martin Buckley. After going into sudden heart failure, gaining seven stone from fear, and battl Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 05:52, 27 Aug 2026 Martin Buckley's story is the fourteenth in the Manchester Evening News' Survivors series, featuring interviews with remarkable people who have survived traumatic experiences Many never get the chance to hear terrifying news, doctors told Martin. Back in 2019, aged 35, he and his wife had offered to take a friend's young son for a day out at a soft play centre in Manchester - as they often did Amid the children's laughter and noise, he began to feel as though something wasn't quite right. "He was off playing," Martin said. "I'd gone back to my wife, got drinks or something, and then I went back to find him "And as I've seen him, I've gone towards him, and I've ducked under a bridge that was in there. As soon as I kind of bent down to go underneath it, something just happened in my heart." Martin, who works in IT for the NHS, describes the sensation as his heart 'skipping a beat', adding: "I didn't feel great so I went back to my wife and I'm like, I don't feel good, I don't feel right."

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Drug dealer shot by police as they swooped after carrying out surveillance Lewis Hanson was blasted to the elbow News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 18:09, 26 Aug 2026 Updated 18:13, 26 Aug 2026 View 2 Images (Image: Supplied) A drug dealer was shot by armed police as they swooped on him after carrying out surveillance Lewis Hanson, 20, was blasted to the elbow by an armed officer in Whitefield , Bury , after the cop ‘felt compelled’ to discharge his firearm. Police later discovered a converted gun in a flat in Radcliffe where Hanson stored cocaine and cannabis for onward sale Previously, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said it has launched an investigation into the firearms operation which ended in Hanson being shot During a sentencing hearing today, (August 26) Manchester Crown Court heard that Hanson, now 20, has been dealing cannabis since the age of 14, and had been trying to sell the gun prior to its seizure He will learn his fate tomorrow (August 27) after pleading guilty to drug and firearms charges. Another man, Paul Houghton, 40, who allowed Hanson to use his flat to store the drugs, was handed a suspended prison sentence

Trafford council and developer Bruntwood have now announced a new £2.5m project to expand Foundation, which was completed in the Stamford Quarter in 2024 The building, which was once occupied by House of Fraser, is now a ‘collaborative workspace and leisure destination’. Tyreece Bedford, 22, found himself in the dock following the 'tomfoolery' last summer Manchester Crown Court heard a man he knew cycled past him on Pilkington Way, Radcliffe , on June 14, 2025. The cyclist turned back and approached Bedford The pair briefly spoke before Bedford took the man's hat. When he tried to get it back, Bedford brandished an object cops believe was a blade CCTV footage played in court showed the man backing away from Bedford. He was initially charged with threatening a person with a blade and theft, but instead pleaded guilty to the lesser charge of affray Prosecutor Brian Berlyne said: "The man backed away in apparent fear. He appears to believe it to be a weapon. Police believe it to have been a small knife."

candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

candidates.evidence_text: The University of Manchester community has expressed its sincere thanks for overwhelming show of support by leading figures from science, culture and public life in support of Jodrell Bank In recent weeks, a range of open letters have been published highlighting the importance of Jodrell Bank, e-MERLIN and the wider radio astronomy capabilities based at the Observatory. Support has come from leading figures in science, culture and public life, as well as from organ Lending their voices to support the positive impact, which the whole of the Jodrell Bank site has given to UK science and culture, signatories include Professor Brian Cox, Sir Brian May, Tim Peake, Chris Hadfield, Professor Jim Al-Khalili, Simon Armitage, Johnny Marr, members of Alongside this, letters have been received from international research organisations, observatory directors, scientific advisory groups and astronomy institutes from across the UK and Europe. candidates.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

candidates.evidence_text: A new strategy aims to help everyone in Bolton live a healthy, connected and fulfilling life, supported by strong communities, active environments and quality homes The Joint Local Health and Wellbeing (JHWS) Strategy 2026–2029 sets out how organisations across the borough will work together to improve health and wellbeing and reduce health inequalities The strategy has been approved by Bolton's Health and Wellbeing Board, which brings together leaders from local government, public health, social care, the NHS, housing, the voluntary and community sector, and other key partners The strategy places a strong emphasis on prevention, recognising that helping people stay healthy is just as important as treating illness when it occurs It provides a shared framework for partners to take collective action on the factors that have the biggest impact on people's health and wellbeing The Health and Wellbeing Board has identified three priorities where its collective leadership can add the greatest value

candidates.lead: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović .
candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. candidates.evidence_text: Grub on the Docks - Media City UK Street Food Line-Up: Featuring Sizzling Seoul, Dukes Po Boys, and more Grub on the Docks Venue Gardens Dates 28 th May - 20 th Sep '26 Open Tuesday to Sunday weekly, 12 noon – 10pm GRUB on the Docks is bringing the flavour this summer – think unreal street food, ice-cold drinks and non-stop vibes right in the MediaCity gardens, on the waterfront. We’re talking a stacked rotation of indie food like Sizzling Seoul, Umami Cartel, Oppa Korean Dogs and more, switching it up every week so there’s always something new to try. NEW challenge, take on the BELLY BUSTER CHALLENGE from CAFF – sausage. bacon. egg. black pudding. hash brown. All packed into one proper Belly Buster bap for £7.50. Time to beat is 5 minutes set the fastest finishing time and your next Belly Buster is FREE . EVENTS Wine on the Docks Every Wednesday | All day, venue hours Midweek just got better. Every Wednesday, buy two glasses of the same wine and we’ll top up the rest of the bottle on us. No catch, no fuss just a proper reason to make Wednesday your new favourite day. Sunset Sessions Every Friday | 5–8pm Clock off and head straight to the water’s edge. A rotating line-up of DJs kicks off the weekend early, with a trader special and a featured drinks offer to match. Same time, same spot, every Friday, your after-work wind-down sorted. Paws on the Docks 8 AUGUST | 22 AUGUST | 5 SEPTEMBER | 19 SEPTEMBER | Mornings Bring the dog, grab a coffee, make a morning of it. Paws on the Docks is our relaxed dog-friendly social – think breakfast specials, water bowls, complimentary pup cups and market stalls that welcome four-legged visitors as warmly as the two-legged ones. Residents social Thursday 20th August – 5pm to 7pm An evening for all MediaCity residents, with a DJ playing live on the docks. A nice informal social, come down, grab a drink and meet other residents at our waterfront setting. Media Makers Mixer Thursday 27th August – 5pm to 7pm A regular hosted networking event for MediaCity’s creative and production community, designed to bring people together and encourage connections across the area. Be the first in the know Sign up to receive email updates on the latest events, news and offers at MediaCity Visit our privacy policy here. Welcome to The Bolly-woods, where the dancing is non-stop, the drama is bigger than your aunties, and the romance is straight out of a filmi blockbuster! Meet Surinder, sweet, strong, and stuck in a never-ending chore list thanks to her two Insta-fame obsessed stepsisters, Lovely and Bubbly. Her only real support? The Palace Theatre of Varieties opened on Whit Monday 1891 and cost its owners the then colossal sum of £40,500. In the late 1970’s the Palace Theatre underwent a major refurbishment and re-opened in 1981 with Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Jesus Christ Superstar and has since then retained its position as the premier provincial touring venue

evidence_packet.evidence_text: For two decades Sounds From The Other City has been championing new music, local promoters and the off-kilter beauty of Salford, the oft-overlooked ‘other city’ to Manchester The unique model of SFTOC means that the festival curation is ever-evolving; each year the festival invites a selection of the region’s best promoters and selectors, give them a stage and ask them to book the artists that most excite them The festival has hosted early-day performances from artists as diverse as Black Country, New Road, The Ting Tings, Alabaster de Plume, Alt-J, The Ting Tings, BiPolar Sunshine, Hannah Peel, GoGo Penguin right through to 2017’s Mercury Music Prize winner Sampha, BBC Sound of 2018 n Join in for another round of Sounds From The Other City, celebrating the very best in new music, performance and art General release tickets are on sale now and going fast. Get yours below and join the party of the year on this May Day Bank Holiday Sunday Chapel Street and the Crescent neighbourhood - see SFTOC website for all venues taking part

candidates.evidence_text: Totally Stockport has launched a new masterplan as part of its Going Green programme, setting out a bold and practical vision for a greener, healthier and more vibrant town centre Developed by Layer.studio in consultation with retailers and residents, ‘Going Green’ focuses on the places people use every day and sets out a strategy, toolkit and initial projects to support regeneration, wellbeing and economic activity With the aim to create a connected, people-focused green infrastructure network, streets, squares and key routes have been reviewed to create a one connected green network The masterplan spans the 80Ha Totally Stockport BID Boundary and combines quick wins with longer-term visions in key areas, setting out a practical route to a town centre that’s even more walkable, attractive and economically active Paul Kelsall, BID Director at Totally Stockport and co-owner of Stockport based Kelsall Architects, said: “At its core, ‘Going Green’ is about joining the green dots “From Merseyway to the Underbanks and Chestergate, the masterplan shows how simple, well-placed changes such as more planting and enhanced greenery can change the face of the town centre

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Totally Stockport has launched a new masterplan as part of its Going Green programme, setting out a bold and practical vision for a greener, healthier and more vibrant town centre Developed by Layer.studio in consultation with retailers and residents, ‘Going Green’ focuses on the places people use every day and sets out a strategy, toolkit and initial projects to support regeneration, wellbeing and economic activity With the aim to create a connected, people-focused green infrastructure network, streets, squares and key routes have been reviewed to create a one connected green network The masterplan spans the 80Ha Totally Stockport BID Boundary and combines quick wins with longer-term visions in key areas, setting out a practical route to a town centre that’s even more walkable, attractive and economically active Paul Kelsall, BID Director at Totally Stockport and co-owner of Stockport based Kelsall Architects, said: “At its core, ‘Going Green’ is about joining the green dots “From Merseyway to the Underbanks and Chestergate, the masterplan shows how simple, well-placed changes such as more planting and enhanced greenery can change the face of the town centre

candidates.evidence_text: SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Digital, cyber & AI SafetyCulture marks 10 years in Manchester with Mitti rebrand and new AI capabilities Published on August 21, 2026 News Global operations system SafetyCulture is celebrating 10 years of business in Manchester with the biggest transformation in its history, including a rebrand and new AI capabilities. SafetyCulture today rebrands as Mitti, a new identity signalling its expansion beyond traditional safety management to an all-in-one operations system for the frontline. The word Mitti means “middle” — the centre of an operation, where decisions get made, and work happens. The platform connects the people on the frontline with those making decisions in the boardroom. After launching in Manchester in 2016, Mitti expanded into a 10,000 sq ft office at Bond on Mosley Street in 2024 as its EMEA headquarters. During the decade, Mitti has built a UK customer base of 18,000 organisations, including Unilever, DHL, H&M, Domino’s Pizza, and Network Rail. Celebrating the milestone, Dawid Jaworski, EMEA Lead at Mitti, says : “Ten years ago we were a handful of people in a small Manchester office trying to convince businesses that the clipboard had had its day. A decade on, this city is the base from which we serve the entire EMEA region. “The customers we serve are the industries this region was built on. That proximity matters. Being surrounded by it keeps us honest about who we’re building for. “The city has grown up alongside us. Manchester is now the UK’s largest tech economy outside London with more than 10,000 tech businesses operating here. We built our first decade in Manchester, and we’re building the next one here too.” The platform is used by the workers who don’t sit at a desk — 80%¹ of the world’s workforce — across manufacturing, construction, retail, quick-service restaurants (QSR), energy and other industries. Among its North West customers is Bury-headquartered structural steelwork firm William Hare, which has completed more than 180,000 inspections on the platform, saved over a million sheets of paper, and standardised more than 500 templates across its sites while remaining audit-ready. The rebrand lands as UK operators face a tightening compliance picture. Martyn’s Law will require premises with a capacity of 200 or more to document emergency procedures and train staff accordingly, with enforcement expected from spring 2027. In construction, the Building Safety Act has raised the bar on inspection records, contractor oversight and evidence trails. Jaworski adds : “Every day, more than 3.4 million images and 380,000 inspections are added to our platform — captured by people on site, mid-shift, doing the actual work. That’s ground truth others can’t replicate. It’s the difference between software that guesses what’s happening on the frontline and software that knows.” The tools meant to help teams meet these obligations are falling short, according to Mitti. Only around one-third of frontline supervisors find their digital tools “very effective,” 2 according to a commissioned study conducted by Forrester Consulting on behalf of Mitti. Central to the new Mitti platform is its ‘5 Star Benchmarking’ capability, which turns years of operational history into one clear score for multi-site operators, showing how each location is performing and, more importantly, how to improve. The platform’s new AI capabilities are built on that same frontline data. Agents gather intelligence and automate processes; AI Assistant surfaces patterns and risks, compares performance against relevant standards and regulations, creates action plans and answers questions in seconds. And AI Issue Creation turns a photo, prompt or voice note into a ready-to-review issue. It blends village charm with urban convenience and a vibrant community atmosphere. It boasts gorgeous historic buildings alongside a whole network of trendy, independent hospitality and retail businesses. And it Hidden beneath the surface of all this are stories. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: Taking place ahead of Manchester Pride, Ferocious Cabaret feels like an ideal way to kick off the city's wider celebrations HOME Manchester , Manchester 27 August 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester’s queer cabaret scene has long been one of the city’s most vibrant creative communities, blurring the boundaries between theatre, dance, circus and live art. This August, Ferocious Cabaret takes over HOME for a one-night celebration of the city’s thriving queer perform Behind the glitter and glamour is a project rooted in Manchester’s creative community. Presented by House of Pantha, Ferocious Cabaret is the culmination of an artist development programme led by acclaimed burlesque performer Cleopantha in collaboration with Darren Pritchard of G Expect an eclectic mix of burlesque, boylesque, drag and circus, with performances ranging from seductive and theatrical to bold, high-energy and unapologetically queer. Together, they reflect the creativity, confidence and diversity that continue to define Manchester’s thriving Whether you’re a long-time cabaret fan or discovering the art form for the first time, Ferocious Cabaret offers the chance to discover new performers, celebrate established talent and immerse yourself in one of Manchester’s most exciting creative communities

Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. evidence_packet.evidence_text: As AI adoption gathers pace, organisations are under growing pressure to invest and demonstrate where the technology can deliver meaningful business value This lunchtime session brings together senior technology leaders with first-hand experience of putting AI into practice. Drawing on real-world examples and lessons from delivery, the panel will explore what it takes to move from ambition and experimentation to measurable results The discussion will offer a candid view of the decisions, foundations and trade-offs involved. Speakers will share what they have learned from implementing AI, including the technical, operational and organisational challenges encountered along the way There will also be an opportunity to put your questions to the panel and connect with fellow technology leaders over lunch 📅 Date: Thursday 1st October 2026 🕒 Time: 12pm-2pm 📍 Location: No.1 Circle Square 💷 Price: Manchester Digital members - Free (4 x tickets per company) Non members - £30 Spaces are limited - secure your place to gain insight from these senior leaders and connect with peers

candidates.summary: FREE monthly business support sessions with expert local partners helping Stockport businesses start, grow and thrive! Are you looking for expert advice to start or grow your business?
candidates.lead: FREE monthly business support sessions with expert local partners helping Stockport businesses start, grow and thrive!
candidates.practical_angle: Проверьте бесплатную регистрацию и подходит ли формат для профессионального нетворка.
candidates.evidence_text: GM Business Growth Hub | FREE BUSINESS ADVICE @ One Stockport Business Support Hub Please ensure Javascript is enabled for purposes of website accessibility Home Events FREE BUSINESS ADVICE @ One Stockport Business Support Hub 28.08.2026 FREE BUSINESS ADVICE @ One Stockport Business Support Hub Date: 28 August 2026 End Date: 28 August 2026 Location: Merseyway Innovation Centre, Stockport Time: 10am-4pm Theme: Growth Register FREE monthly business support sessions with expert local partners helping Stockport businesses start, grow and thrive! Are you looking for expert advice to start or grow your business? Join us for our monthly Business Support Hub at the Merseyway Innovation Centre. When: Last Friday of every month Where: Merseyway Innovation Centre, Stockport Whether you're at the idea stage, ready to scale up, or looking to access funding, training, or innovation support, our free sessions connect you with a variety of local experts and partners. What’s on offer? Tailored guidance from your local business support network: Stockport Council, GM Business Growth Hub, Enterprising You, GM Libraries Build-A-Business and Stockport College. Advice on all your business growth needs: Self-employed, start-up, funding, business planning, training opportunities, innovation, recruitment and retention, sales and marketing, and more. Access to further fully funded support opportunities and programmes for business success. A welcoming space to connect with professionals who understand your challenges and goals. Spend the day: Join the community of like-minded professionals. Merseyway Innovation Centre is a hub of creativity and enterprise and drop-in coworking is available at £15 for the day. (To find out more and book a desk: Coworking Space in Stockport | Flexible Workspace | Innovate Stockport ) How it works: Book a free one-hour session with business support advisors for personalised advice. Prefer flexibility? Just drop in and chat with the experts available. Why attend? Access free, high-quality support from a network of trusted partners. Get practical advice tailored to your business needs. Build connections that can help you take your next steps with confidence. Who’s it for? Startups and pre-start businesses Established businesses of any size or sector Entrepreneurs with a good idea! Don’t miss out! Secure your spot or learn more by booking your free session now. Walk-ins are welcome, but booking ensures you get dedicated one-on-one time with our experts. Can't make our August session? Book a date that suits you in your calendar: https://tinyurl.com/5jh26742 Any questions?: Please contact economyWS@stockport.gov.uk Book your session today – let’s help your business thrive.
